subject: Partner retainer reconciliation & lead registration clarity
messages:
From: Samir Nair <samir@aperture.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example
Cc: contracts@aperture.ai
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Partner commercial + onboarding retainer questions

Laura — great to meet you last week. Per our conversation, we're trying to close commercial terms so we can start engineering work in August. A couple items where we need explicit confirmation from Redwood before our execs sign off: 

1) Upfront retainer / credit: Aperture typically pays an upfront partner retainer. We expect that to be treated as a credit against first-quarter consumption charges rather than a separate non-refundable fee. Can Redwood confirm whether the retainer will be applied as credits, and how any unused balance is reconciled?

2) Lead registration window and proof of intro: We need clarity on lead registration duration and what qualifies as proof-of-intro. Aperture's competitors require 6 months; our legal team would prefer a 180-day window if possible. We can provide HubSpot IDs or an introduction email chain as proof.

3) Prorated onboarding credits: If a customer signs mid-quarter and uses Redwood for 40% of the quarter, can Aperture's retainer be prorated against the actual usage billing period?

Attached is a draft SOW and a short proposed credit table to show how we'd like credits to apply. Can you loop in legal and provide a redline of the MSA (we have a few standard clauses to propose)?

Thanks — would like to have a term-sheet confirmed by next week if possible.

— Samir
Aperture Analytics

Attachments: Aperture_draft_SOW.pdf (attachment stub), proposed-credit-table.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.example
To: Samir Nair <samir@aperture.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner commercial + onboarding retainer questions

Samir — thanks and glad we're moving quickly. Quick answers and suggested path forward below.

1) Retainer treatment: Redwood treats partner retainers as a credit against invoiced consumption for the first 3 billing periods by default (typically 90 days). Unused balance after that period is returned or can be applied to a future invoice with mutual agreement. We can be flexible on the length if there's a strong case to extend.

2) Lead registration window: Our standard is 90 days for a clean registration (to balance stale introductions and long nurture cycles). Proof-of-intro is the HubSpot contact ID or an email thread from the partner to the prospect that predates Redwood outreach. We require the proof to be logged in our partner portal before the first demo or technical touch.

3) Prorated credits: We support prorated application of retainers for mid-quarter go-lives. The partner-proposed spreadsheet is helpful — legal will want a simple formula (retainer * days_active_in_billing_period / total_days_in_period). We'll convert the example into clause language in the MSA redline.

Proposed compromise given Aperture's ask: Redwood can consider a 120-day registration window (instead of 90) for strategic partners with an upfront retainer > $25k. That would be a stated carve-out in Schedule A.

Next steps: 
- I'm attaching our partner playbook (v2) which documents the registration process and approved proof types.
- Ben and Marissa are cc'd to validate payout cadence and tracking. Ben: can you confirm revenue-share cadence (monthly payout vs. quarterly net-recognition) and whether we can add a note to handle proration on mid-quarter starts?
- I'll ask Legal to return an MSA redline by Friday with the Schedule A carve-out language.

If that sounds reasonable, let's lock a 30-minute call tomorrow to agree on the 120-day compromise and any thresholds.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.example

Attachments: Redwood_partner_playbook_v2.pdf (attachment stub)
Related: https://drive.google.com/redwood/partner-playbook-v2

From: Samir Nair <samir@aperture.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.example
Cc: contracts@aperture.ai
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner commercial + onboarding retainer questions

Laura — appreciate the fast reply and the playbook. A few clarifications from our side: 

• 120 days is closer to what we need, thank you. Aperture's sales cycle typically runs longer in regulated industries; 180 days is our preference for large-enterprise sourced introductions (>$250k ACV). Can Redwood accept a tiered window: 120 days for standard introductions, 180 days for enterprise deals above a threshold?

• On proration: we prefer the retainer to be applied pro rata to the customer's first 12 weeks of consumption, not necessarily by calendar quarter days — this maps better to our sales ramp and implementation cadence. Would Redwood accept a 12-week lookback model (i.e., retainer credits applied against first 12 weeks of invoices)?

I've attached a redline of the SOW with how Aperture typically structures retainer credits and an example schedule. If legal is able to take the 120/180 tier as a draft carve-out, we can proceed to countersign quickly.

— Samir

Attachments: Aperture_redline_SOW.pdf (attachment stub)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.example
To: Samir Nair <samir@aperture.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Partner commercial + onboarding retainer questions

Samir — thanks for the specifics. We've discussed internally and propose the following compromise so we can move to signatures next week: 

• Registration window: 120 days standard, with an enterprise carve-out of 180 days for introductions that meet a defined ACV threshold (we propose $200k ACV to align incentives). Aperture can flag those deals in the partner portal at registration time and include the HubSpot ID.

• Proration approach: Redwood will accept a 12-week consumption lookback for applying retainer credits (matches your ask). Legal will translate this into Schedule A language: "retainer credits apply against the customer's first 12 weeks of billed usage following go-live; any unused retainer after 12 weeks is refundable or applied by mutual written agreement."

• Revenue-share payout cadence: Ben, please confirm, but our standard remains monthly bookkeeping with payouts quarterly net-recognition for revenue that requires invoicing adjustments. We can move to monthly cash payouts for partners who opt into net-settlement communications.

Next steps: Ben and Marissa to confirm payout cadence and whether a monthly cash payout option needs additional KYC/ops steps. I'll ask Legal to issue the MSA redline with Schedule A (120/180 days + 12-week lookback) by end of day Friday. After countersign, propose kickoff the following Monday.

If that works, I'll share the updated MSA and the partner portal registration checklist.

Best,
Laura
